name: Superior Bread Puddings
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: one and one-half cupfuls of white sugar
ingredients.originalText: one and one-half cupfuls of white sugar

ingredients.name: fine, dry bread crumbs
ingredients.originalText: two cupfuls of fine, dry bread crumbs

ingredients.name: fresh rich milk
ingredients.originalText: one quart of fresh rich milk

ingredients.name: half a cupful of jelly or jam
ingredients.originalText: half a cupful of jelly or jam
ingredients.quantityText: half a cupful of jelly or jam

instructions.text: Rub the butter into a cupful of sugar
Beat the yolks very light, and stir these together to a cream
Add the bread crumbs soaked in milk, then the flavoring
Bake in a buttered pudding-dish--a large one and but two-thirds full--until the custard is "set"
Draw to the mouth of the oven, spread over with jam or other nice fruit conserve
Cover this with a meringue made of the whipped whites and half a cupful of sugar
Shut the oven and bake until the meringue begins to color

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Rub the butter into a cupful of sugar
2. Beat the yolks very light, and stir these together to a cream
3. Add the bread crumbs soaked in milk, then the flavoring
4. Bake in a buttered pudding-dish--a large one and but two-thirds full--until the custard is "set"
5. Draw to the mouth of the oven, spread over with jam or other nice fruit conserve
6. Cover this with a meringue made of the whipped whites and half a cupful of sugar
7. Shut the oven and bake until the meringue begins to color
8. Eat cold with cream
